source.title: Extensions of tautological rings and motivic structures in the cohomology of M̄_{g,n}
source.authors: Samir Canning, Hannah Larson, Sam Payne
source.read: arXiv v3 (25 October 2024), 33 pages, described by the authors as the final version to appear in Forum of Mathematics, Pi. Read in the LaTeX source of that version (arXiv e-print of 2307.08830v3, file STEForumPiRevision.tex, sha256 of the source archive 7828f493e9e3f26f141687381b26e379d8d5f56319351a525d4d34ed6b8bd391), fetched 22 September 2026. readSections: 2 Preliminaries (2.1 Preliminaries on STEs, 2.2 Pure cohomology in genus 1 and 2)
5 The CKgP in genus 7 with at most 3 marked points (5.1 Hyperelliptic and trigonal loci, 5.2 The tetragonal locus, 5.3 The pentagonal locus)
6 Applications to even cohomology (6.1 degree 4, 6.2 low degree even homology)
7 The thirteenth and fifteenth homology (7.1 Thirteenth homology, 7.2 Fifteenth homology)

summary: Canning, Larson and Payne introduce semi-tautological extensions (STEs): collections of subrings of H^*(M̄_{g,n}) that contain the tautological rings and are closed under the tautological operations that raise dimension — pullback along forgetting and permuting markings, and pushforward along gluing. They prove that in each degree k a single finitely generated STE, with explicit bounds on the generators, contains H^k(M̄_{g,n}) for all g and n, so only finitely many simple motives occur in each degree. Combining this with a new technical tool — if a smooth open substack of a smooth proper Deligne–Mumford stack has the Chow–Künneth generation Property, then its lowest-weight cohomology W_kH^k is generated by algebraic cycle classes, hence vanishes for odd k and is Hodge–Tate for even k — they determine the Hodge structures and Galois representations in H^k(M̄_{g,n}) for k = 13, 14 and 15, confirming the predictions of Chenevier and Lannes in these weights; they show that H^4(M̄_{g,n}) is tautological for all g and n, confirming a prediction of Arbarello and Cornalba, that H^6 is tautological for g ≥ 10, and that H_k is tautological for even k ≤ 14; and they show that H_{13} and H_{15} lie in the STEs generated by the cohomology of M̄_{1,11} and M̄_{1,15}. The base cases require new geometry in genus 7: for n ≤ 3, M_{7,n} has the Chow–Künneth generation Property and R^*(M_{7,n}) = A^*(M_{7,n}), proved by a gonality stratification, Hurwitz stacks with Casnati–Ekedahl bundles for the tetragonal locus, and a new marked version of Mukai's model of pentagonal genus 7 curves as linear sections of the orthogonal Grassmannian OG(5,10) in its spinor embedding. The atlas contains nothing about moduli of curves: no M_{g,n}, no tautological rings, no Chow rings of stacks, no cycle class map to weight-graded cohomology, no Borel–Moore homology, no symplectic local systems, no Brill–Noether theory. What it does have, and what this paper should import, is stable pointed curves (Tau Ceti Stable reduction), algebraic stacks and Grassmann bundles (AlgebraicModuliForArithmeticGeometry), Chow groups and Chern classes (SchemeAndStackFoundations SF.5), cycle classes and realisations (MotivesAndAlgebraicCycles), Hodge structures (Tau Ceti Hodge structures) and the Galois representations of level-one cusp forms (AutomorphicGaloisRepresentations R19.1).

items.name: Stable n-pointed curves
items.statement: A stable n-pointed curve of genus g over a base is a connected nodal curve of arithmetic genus g with n distinct smooth marked points whose every component has finitely many automorphisms fixing the marked points and nodes; equivalently ω_C(Σ p_i) is ample. Stability requires 2g − 2 + n > 0.
items.locator: arXiv:2307.08830v3 (25 October 2024), Throughout; the objects parametrised by M̄_{g,n}
items.note: Prestable, semistable, stable and pointed curves are planned in the Tau Ceti StableReduction roadmap (Layer 3), with marked stabilisation in Layer 9.

items.name: The moduli stacks M_{g,n} and M̄_{g,n}
items.statement: M_{g,n} is the moduli stack of smooth n-pointed genus g curves and M̄_{g,n} its Deligne–Mumford compactification by stable n-pointed curves; M̄_{g,n} is a smooth proper Deligne–Mumford stack over the integers of dimension d_{g,n} = 3g − 3 + n, and M_{g,n} ⊂ M̄_{g,n} is the open locus of smooth curves with complement the boundary ∂M_{g,n}.
items.note: Nothing in the atlas constructs the moduli stack of curves: searches of every stage description return no hit for 'moduli of curves', 'M_{g,n}', 'tautological ring' or 'universal curve' outside the modular-curve roadmaps. R09.4 plans algebraic stacks in the class needed for generalised elliptic curves and polarised abelian schemes, not this one.

items.name: Tautological morphisms and the boundary
items.statement: The tautological morphisms between the M̄_{g,n} are those that forget a marked point, permute the marked points, or glue two marked points (on one curve or on two curves). The boundary ∂M_{g,n} = M̄_{g,n} \ M_{g,n} is the image of the gluing maps; its normalisation ∂̃M_{g,n} is the disjoint union, over stable graphs with one edge, of the corresponding products of moduli spaces modulo automorphisms of the graph.
items.note: These morphisms, the stable graphs indexing the boundary strata and the description of each stratum as a finite quotient of a product of M_{g',n'} with (g',n') ≺ (g,n) are the combinatorial engine of every induction in the paper.

items.name: Tautological rings of M̄_{g,n} and of M_{g,n}
items.statement: RH^*(M̄_{g,n}) ⊂ H^*(M̄_{g,n}) is the smallest collection of subrings closed under pushforward and pullback for all tautological morphisms; R^*(M_{g,n}) ⊂ A^*(M_{g,n}) denotes the subring of the Chow ring generated by tautological cycle classes, and RH^*(M_{g,n}) its image in cohomology.
items.note: The tautological ring is the central object of the subject and is planned nowhere in the atlas.

items.name: ψ-classes, κ-classes and the Hodge bundle
items.statement: On M̄_{g,n}, ψ_i is the first Chern class of the cotangent line at the i-th marking, the κ-classes are pushforwards of powers of ψ from the universal curve, and the Hodge bundle is f_*ω_f for the universal curve f : C → M̄_{g,n}; these generate the tautological classes.
items.locator: arXiv:2307.08830v3 (25 October 2024), Sections 3, 5 and 6 (used throughout; c_1(α_n^*L_i) = −ψ_i in Lemma 5.15)
items.note: The standard generators of the tautological ring; not planned in the atlas.

items.name: Cohomology with its Hodge structure and Galois action
items.statement: H^*(X) denotes rational singular cohomology of a scheme or Deligne–Mumford stack X with its mixed Hodge structure or its ℓ-adic Galois representation, and H^*(X)^{ss} the semi-simplification; W_• is the weight filtration, and W_kH^k(X) ⊂ H^k(X) is the lowest weight part, which for X smooth is the image of H^k of any smooth compactification.
items.locator: arXiv:2307.08830v3 (25 October 2024), Introduction, paragraph before Theorem 1.1
items.note: Mixed Hodge structures with their weight filtration and strictness are planned in the Tau Ceti HodgeStructures roadmap (L2), pure Hodge structures and polarisation in L0 and L1. The ℓ-adic realisation and its semi-simplification are planned in MotivesAndAlgebraicCycles MC.2 and in the Galois-representation roadmaps.

items.name: The Lefschetz motive and the motives of level-one cusp forms
items.statement: L := H^2(P^1) is the Lefschetz object, and S_12 := H^{11}(M̄_{1,11}) and S_16 := W_{15}H^{15}(M_{1,15}) are the two-dimensional motives attached to the level-one cusp forms of weight 12 and 16; a summand L^a S_b of H^*(M̄_{g,n})^{ss} means a Tate twist of that motive.
items.locator: arXiv:2307.08830v3 (25 October 2024), Introduction, paragraph before Theorem 1.1, and Lemma 8.3
items.note: The Galois representation attached to a level-one cusp form of weight ≥ 2 is planned at AutomorphicGaloisRepresentations R19.1 (Kuga–Sato construction) and Mathlib has cusp forms as such; the identification of S_12 with H^{11}(M̄_{1,11}) and of S_16 with the weight 15 cohomology of M_{1,15} is what this paper uses and is not planned.

items.name: Galois representations attached to level-one cusp forms
items.statement: To a cuspidal eigenform of level one and weight k ≥ 2 one attaches a two-dimensional ℓ-adic Galois representation, with the unramified characteristic polynomial given by the Eichler–Shimura relation, and a corresponding pure Hodge structure of weight k − 1.
items.locator: arXiv:2307.08830v3 (25 October 2024), Introduction and Lemma 8.3 (the objects S_12 and S_16)
items.note: R19.1 plans the classical construction, including the higher-weight case through symmetric-power or Kuga–Sato cohomology. Mathlib has modular and cusp forms as such (ModularForm, CuspForm), but not their Galois representations.

items.name: The right-exact boundary sequence
items.statement: For 2g − 2 + n > 0 the sequence H^{k-2}(∂̃M_{g,n}) → H^k(M̄_{g,n}) → W_kH^k(M_{g,n}) → 0 is exact, where the first map is Gysin pushforward from the normalised boundary and the second is restriction.
items.note: The exact sequence that makes every induction on (g, n) work: a class on M̄_{g,n} is boundary-pushed-forward up to its restriction to the open part.

items.name: The Borel–Moore boundary sequence
items.statement: With H^{BM}_k denoting Borel–Moore homology with its mixed Hodge structure or Galois action, the sequence H_k(∂̃M_{g,n}) → H_k(M̄_{g,n}) → W_{-k}H^{BM}_k(M_{g,n}) → 0 is exact for all k.
items.note: The homological counterpart of the previous item, used for Theorems 1.5(3), 1.6 and 1.7.

items.name: The subspaces Φ and Ψ and the partial order on (g, n)
items.statement: With π_i : M_{g,n} → M_{g,n-1} forgetting the i-th marking, Φ^k_{g,n} := Σ_i π_i^*W_kH^k(M_{g,n-1}) ⊂ W_kH^k(M_{g,n}) and Ψ^k_{g,n} := Σ_i ψ_i Φ^{k-2}_{g,n} ⊂ W_kH^k(M_{g,n}). One writes (g', n') ≺ (g, n) when g' ≤ g, 2g' + n' ≤ 2g + n and (g', n') ≠ (g, n); every boundary stratum of M̄_{g,n} is a finite quotient of a product of M_{g',n'} with (g', n') ≺ (g, n).
items.note: The bookkeeping for the inductions; Φ collects what comes from fewer markings and Ψ what comes from fewer markings after multiplication by ψ-classes.

items.name: Chow groups of algebraic stacks and exterior products
items.statement: For algebraic stacks of finite type over a field that are stratified by quotient stacks, A_*(X) denotes the (Edidin–Graham/Kresch) Chow groups, with proper pushforward, flat pullback, excision for open–closed decompositions, the projection formula, Chern classes and the exterior product A_*(X) ⊗ A_*(Y) → A_*(X × Y).
items.locator: arXiv:2307.08830v3 (25 October 2024), Section 4 (the setting of the Chow–Künneth generation Property)
items.note: SF.5 plans Chow groups, rational equivalence, pushforward and pullback, refined Gysin maps, Chern classes and intersection products for schemes; the extension to algebraic stacks stratified by quotient stacks, which the whole of Sections 4 and 5 works in, belongs to the same layer and is not planned.

items.name: The cycle class map
items.statement: For a smooth variety or Deligne–Mumford stack X over the complex numbers there is a cycle class map cl : A_i(X) → W_{2i}H^{2i}(X) landing in the lowest weight part, compatible with proper pushforward, flat pullback, products and Tate twists; algebraic classes are of Hodge type (p, p) and, on the ℓ-adic side, Tate.
items.note: MC.2 plans realisation functors and the compatibility of cycle classes with composition, cup products, pushforward, trace and Tate twists; the version for smooth non-proper targets landing in the weight-graded piece, which this paper needs, belongs to that layer.

items.name: Poincaré duality on a smooth proper Deligne–Mumford stack
items.statement: For M̄_{g,n} smooth and proper of dimension d_{g,n}, cup product induces a perfect pairing H^k(M̄_{g,n}) × H^{2d_{g,n}-k}(M̄_{g,n}) → Q identifying H_k(M̄_{g,n}) with H^{2d_{g,n}-k}(M̄_{g,n}) as Q-vector spaces, and compatibly with Hodge structures and Galois actions up to Tate twist; hard Lefschetz gives the injections used for top-heaviness.
items.locator: arXiv:2307.08830v3 (25 October 2024), Introduction (the identification H_k = H^{2d−k}) and Sections 6–8
items.note: Sheaf cohomology with compact support and duality on schemes are planned at SF.2; hard Lefschetz at DWP.9; polarisation and Hodge–Riemann on the Hodge side at HodgeStructures L1. The Deligne–Mumford stack case is used throughout the paper without comment.

items.name: Motivic structures in H^13, H^14 and H^15 of M̄_{g,n}
items.note: The main theorem: it confirms the predictions of Chenevier and Lannes for motivic weights k ≤ 15. The semi-simplification is relevant only for Galois representations, since the Hodge structure on the cohomology of a smooth proper Deligne–Mumford stack is semi-simple.

items.name: Semi-tautological extensions (STEs)
items.statement: A semi-tautological extension is a collection of subrings S^*(M̄_{g,n}) ⊂ H^*(M̄_{g,n}) containing the tautological subrings RH^*(M̄_{g,n}) and closed under pullback by forgetting and permuting marked points and under pushforward for gluing marked points. Examples: RH^*, H^* itself, and the subrings generated by algebraic cycle classes. An intersection of STEs is an STE; an STE is finitely generated if it is the smallest one containing a given finite union of Q-subspaces of ⊔_{g,n} H^*(M̄_{g,n}); it is motivic if each S^*(M̄_{g,n}) is a sub-Hodge structure whose base change to Q_ℓ is Galois stable. For an STE, S_k(M̄_{g,n}) denotes S^{2d_{g,n}-k}(M̄_{g,n}).
items.locator: arXiv:2307.08830v3 (25 October 2024), Definition 1.2 with the surrounding discussion
items.note: The paper's central new notion: a weakening of the tautological formalism that keeps only the operations raising dimension, which is what inductive arguments need.

items.name: Finite generation in each degree
items.statement: For any fixed degree k, the STE generated by {H^{k'}(M̄_{g',n'}) : k' ≤ k, g' < (3/2)k' + 1, n' ≤ k', 4g' − 4 + n' ≥ k'} contains H^k(M̄_{g,n}) for all g and n. In particular there is a finitely generated STE containing H^k(M̄_{g,n}) for all g and n.
items.note: The structural theorem behind every application: in each degree, finitely many explicit base cases generate everything. Its proof combines Lemma 2.1, Lemma 3.1(b), the virtual cohomological dimension 4g − 4 + n of M_{g,n} and Harer–Wahl stability.

items.name: Finiteness of the motives appearing in each degree
items.statement: For each k there are only finitely many isomorphism classes of simple Hodge structures (respectively ℓ-adic Galois representations) in ⊕_{g,n} H^k(M̄_{g,n})^{ss}.
items.note: The qualitative form of Theorem 1.3, and the statement that makes the Chenevier–Lannes predictions checkable degree by degree.

items.name: H^4 of M̄_{g,n} is tautological
items.statement: RH^*(M̄_{g,n}) contains H^4(M̄_{g,n}) for all g and n.
items.note: This confirms a prediction of Arbarello and Cornalba from the 1990s; Polito had proved it for g ≥ 8.

items.name: H^6 of M̄_{g,n} is tautological for g ≥ 10
items.statement: RH^*(M̄_{g,n}) contains H^6(M̄_{g,n}) for g ≥ 10.
items.note: Uses Theorem 1.5(1) for the boundary classes and stability of H^6(M_{g,n}) for g ≥ 10.

items.name: Low even homology of M̄_{g,n} is tautological
items.statement: RH^*(M̄_{g,n}) contains H_k(M̄_{g,n}) for even k ≤ 14, for all g and n; consequently H^k(M̄_{g,n}) ≅ ⊕ L^{k/2} for even k ≤ 14.
items.note: The homological statement that feeds Theorem 1.1 through Poincaré duality.

items.name: Thirteenth homology lies in the STE generated by H^{11}(M̄_{1,11})
items.statement: The STE generated by H^{11}(M̄_{1,11}) contains H_{13}(M̄_{g,n}) for all g and n.
items.note: The first nontrivial extension of the tautological ring handled by the method.

items.name: Fifteenth homology lies in the STE generated by two genus-one groups
items.statement: The STE generated by H^{11}(M̄_{1,11}) and H^{15}(M̄_{1,15}) contains H_{15}(M̄_{g,n}) for all g and n.
items.note: Together with Lemma 8.3 this is what isolates the S_16 contribution and proves that it does not appear for g ≥ 2.

items.name: Conjecture: even cohomology is tautological up to degree 20
items.statement: RH^*(M̄_{g,n}) contains H^k(M̄_{g,n}) for even k ≤ 20.
items.note: True for k ≤ 4, and for k = 6 with g ≥ 10; for k ≤ 14 it is equivalent to perfectness of the pairing RH^k × RH_k. The bound 20 is sharp: Graber–Pandharipande exhibit a non-tautological algebraic class in H^{22}(M̄_{2,20}) and Petersen–Tommasi show the pairing fails to be perfect for k ≥ 22.

items.name: The cohomology of M̄_{3,n} for n ≤ 11
items.statement: For n ≤ 11, H^*(M̄_{3,n})^{ss} is a polynomial in L and S_12.
items.note: Proved from the CKgP for M_{3,n} (Canning–Larson) together with Lemma 4.3; it unconditionally confirms the point-counting computations of Bergström and Faber for n = 9, 10, 11, which were conditional on the Chenevier–Lannes list.

items.name: Genus seven with at most three markings
items.statement: For n ≤ 3, the moduli space M_{7,n} has the Chow–Künneth generation Property and R^*(M_{7,n}) = A^*(M_{7,n}).
items.note: The geometric input needed as a base case; it is proved by a gonality stratification and a new marked version of Mukai's model of pentagonal genus 7 curves.

items.name: STEs are top-heavy and unimodal
items.statement: Any STE satisfies dim S^k(M̄_{g,n}) ≤ dim S_k(M̄_{g,n}) for k ≤ dim M̄_{g,n}, and its dimensions in even and in odd degrees are unimodal, because an STE contains RH^* and hence an ample class, and multiplication by a suitable power of it injects S^k into S_k.
items.note: The elementary structural consequence of containing the tautological ring.

items.name: The filling criterion
items.statement: Let S^* be an STE and 2g − 2 + n > 0. If the canonical map S^{k'}(M̄_{g',n'}) → W_{k'}H^{k'}(M_{g',n'})/(Φ^{k'}_{g',n'} + RH^{k'}(M_{g',n'})) is surjective for (g', n', k') = (g, n, k) and for all (g', n', k') with (g', n') ≺ (g, n), 2d_{g',n'} − k' ≤ 2d_{g,n} − k and k' ≤ k − 2, then S^k(M̄_{g,n}) = H^k(M̄_{g,n}).
items.note: A cohomological analogue of the filling criteria of Canning–Larson. Its proof compares the boundary sequence for S^* with the one for H^*, using the Künneth formula on the normalised boundary and induction along ≺.

items.name: Pure cohomology of M_{1,n} (Getzler)
items.statement: For n ≥ k, a basis of W_kH^k(M_{1,n}) is given by the C(n−1, k−1) pullbacks from W_kH^k(M_{1,A}) over subsets A ⊂ {1, …, n} of size k with 1 ∈ A; consequently there is an S_n-equivariant isomorphism W_kH^k(M_{1,n}) ≅ S_{k+1} ⊗ V_{n-k+1,1^{k-1}}. For n < k, W_kH^k(M_{1,n}) = 0.
items.note: The complete classification of pure cohomology in genus 1, and the source of every S_12 and S_16 in the paper.

items.name: H^{13}(M̄_{1,n}) lies in the STE generated by H^{11}(M̄_{1,11})
items.statement: H^{13}(M̄_{1,n}) lies in the STE generated by H^{11}(M̄_{1,11}) for all n.
items.note: The genus-one base case for Theorem 1.6.

items.name: The cusp-form STE is closed under all tautological operations
items.statement: The STE S_ω^* generated by the classes ω ∈ H^{11}(M̄_{1,11}) is closed under the tautological operations induced by pushforward for forgetting marked points and pullback for gluing marked points, hence under all tautological operations.
items.note: Not every STE is closed under the dimension-lowering operations; the ones studied here are, which is what makes them usable as motivic coefficients.

items.name: The same holds for any collection of cusp-form classes
items.statement: More generally, the Hodge groups H^{k,0}(M̄_{1,k}) correspond to the spaces of cusp forms for SL_2(Z) of weight k + 1, and the STE generated by any subset of these cusp-form spaces is closed under all tautological operations.
items.note: The general principle behind Proposition 2.4.

items.name: Pure even cohomology of M_{2,n} in low degrees
items.note: The genus-two base case for the even statements.

items.name: Low even cohomology of M̄_{2,n} is tautological
items.statement: If k ≤ 10 then H^{2k}(M̄_{2,n}) = RH^{2k}(M̄_{2,n}) for all n.
items.note: Deduced from Proposition 2.6 by the filling criterion.

items.name: Pure odd cohomology of M_{2,n} in degrees 13 and 15
items.statement: In the category of Galois representations, W_{13}H^{13}(M_{2,n})^{ss} ≅ ⊕ L S_12 and W_{15}H^{15}(M_{2,n})^{ss} ≅ ⊕ L^2 S_12.
items.note: The genus-two input that rules out S_16 in degree 15 for g = 2.

items.name: Degrees 13 and 15 on M̄_{2,n}
items.statement: In the category of Galois representations, H^{13}(M̄_{2,n})^{ss} ≅ ⊕ L S_12 and H^{15}(M̄_{2,n})^{ss} ≅ ⊕ L^2 S_12.
items.locator: arXiv:2307.08830v3 (25 October 2024), Corollary 2.9 (with Lemma 8.1 for the Hodge-theoretic analogue)
items.note: The genus-two case of Theorem 1.1.

items.name: Symplectic local systems on M_g
items.statement: For a partition λ = (λ_1 ≥ … ≥ λ_g ≥ 0), V_λ denotes the associated symplectic local system on M_g, of weight |λ| = λ_1 + … + λ_g; when |λ| = n, V_λ also denotes the irreducible S_n-representation indexed by λ, and λ^T the transposed partition.
items.note: The coefficient systems in which the cohomology of M_{g,n} decomposes; not planned in the atlas.

items.name: The quotient by Φ and Ψ is cohomology of local systems
items.statement: (a) If g ≥ 2 then W_kH^k(M_{g,n})/(Φ^k_{g,n} + Ψ^k_{g,n}) ≅ ⊕_{|λ|=n} W_kH^{k-n}(M_g, V_λ) ⊗ V_{λ^T}. (b) If n > 0 and n ≥ k then W_kH^k(M_{g,n}) = Φ^k_{g,n}.
items.note: The key vanishing tool. The proof uses the open inclusion M_{g,n} ⊂ C^n in the n-fold fibre power of the universal curve, the degeneration of the Leray spectral sequence, the Künneth decomposition, and the identification of the summands spanned by Φ̃, Ψ̃ and the diagonal classes with the ones where some i_s is 0, 2 or where two indices are equal.

items.name: Odd numbers of markings in genus two
items.statement: Suppose n is odd. The STE generated by H^k(M̄_{2,n-1}), H^{k-2}(M̄_{2,n-1}) and H^{k-2}(M̄_{1,m}) for m ≤ n + 2 contains H^k(M̄_{2,n}).
items.note: Proved from Lemma 3.1(a) and the fact that the hyperelliptic involution acts on a weight-n local system on M_2 by (−1)^n, so local systems of odd weight have no cohomology.

items.name: The homological analogue of finite generation
items.statement: Analogues of Theorem 1.3 and Lemma 2.1 hold for homology: for each k there is a finitely generated STE containing H_k(M̄_{g,n}) for all g and n, with explicit bounds on the generators.
items.note: The form actually used in Sections 6 and 7.

items.name: Inputs to the finite-generation bound
items.statement: The proof of Theorem 1.3 uses three vanishing statements: W_{k'}H^{k'}(M_{g',n'})/Φ vanishes for n' > k' (Lemma 3.1(b)); H^{k'}(M_{g',n'}) vanishes above the virtual cohomological dimension 4g' − 4 + n' of M_{g',n'}; and H^{k'}(M_{g',n'}) is tautological in the stable range k' ≤ (2g' − 2)/3 by Harer's stability and Wahl's theorem.
items.locator: arXiv:2307.08830v3 (25 October 2024), Proof of Theorem 1.3 in Section 3
items.note: Each of the three is a substantial classical input that the atlas does not plan.

items.name: The Chow–Künneth generation Property
items.statement: A smooth algebraic stack X of finite type over a field, stratified by quotient stacks, has the Chow–Künneth generation Property (CKgP) if for every algebraic stack Y of finite type stratified by quotient stacks the exterior product A_*(X) ⊗ A_*(Y) → A_*(X × Y) is surjective.
items.note: The property that replaces properness in the paper's control of pure cohomology.

items.name: Permanence properties of the CKgP
items.statement: Let X be a smooth algebraic stack of finite type over a field, stratified by quotient stacks. (1) An open substack of a stack with the CKgP has the CKgP. (2) If Y → X is proper, surjective, representable by Deligne–Mumford stacks and Y has the CKgP, then X has the CKgP. (3) If X has a finite stratification by substacks with the CKgP, then X has the CKgP. (4) For an affine bundle V → X, V has the CKgP if and only if X does. (5) If X has the CKgP and G → X is a Grassmann bundle, then G has the CKgP. (6) BGL_n, BSL_n and BPGL_n have the CKgP.
items.note: The calculus by which the CKgP is verified in practice, and the whole content of Section 5's strategy.

items.name: The CKgP makes pure cohomology algebraic
items.statement: Let X be an open substack of a smooth proper Deligne–Mumford stack over the complex numbers. If X has the CKgP then the cycle class map ⊕_i A_i(X) → ⊕_k W_kH^k(X) is surjective; in particular W_kH^k(X) = 0 for k odd and W_kH^k(X) is pure Hodge–Tate for k even.
items.note: The key new technical statement of the paper: it extends to non-proper X the fact that the cycle class map is an isomorphism for smooth proper stacks with the CKgP, and it is what controls the motivic structures in H^k(M̄_{g,n}) for k ≥ 13.

items.name: The ℓ-adic analogue
items.statement: The same argument with Q_ℓ-coefficients gives the corresponding statement for the cycle class map to ℓ-adic étale cohomology over an arbitrary field.
items.note: This is what makes Theorem 1.1 a statement about Galois representations and not only about Hodge structures.

items.name: Pure cohomology of M_{g,n} is tautological in the known CKgP range
items.statement: For all g ≤ 7 and n ≤ c(g) as specified in the paper's Table 1, W_kH^k(M_{g,n}) = RH^k(M_{g,n}); in particular, for k odd and n ≤ c(g), W_kH^k(M_{g,n}) = gr^W_k H^k_c(M_{g,n}) = 0.
items.note: The table of known cases (assembled from Canning–Larson and this paper's Theorem 1.10) that supplies every base case of the inductions in Sections 6–8.

items.name: The gonality stratification of M_{7,n}
items.statement: M_{7,n} is filtered by the loci M^k_{7,n} of curves admitting a degree ≤ k map to P^1, M^2 ⊂ M^3 ⊂ M^4 ⊂ M^5 = M_{7,n}, since a genus 7 curve has gonality at most 5 by Brill–Noether theory. By Proposition 4.2(3) it suffices to prove the CKgP for each stratum M^k_{7,n} \ M^{k-1}_{7,n}, and for the Chow-ring statement it suffices to show that every class supported on M^k is tautological modulo classes supported on M^{k-1}.
items.note: The strategy for Theorem 1.10; the hyperelliptic and trigonal cases (k ≤ 3, n ≤ 14) are quoted from Canning–Larson.

items.name: Hurwitz stacks of tetragonal curves and the Casnati–Ekedahl bundles
items.statement: H_{4,g,n} is the Hurwitz stack of degree 4 covers f : C → P^1 with C smooth of genus g and n marked points, with forgetful map β_n to M_{g,n}; restricting to gonality exactly 4 gives a proper map β'_n : H^◇_{4,g,n} → M_{g,n} \ M^3_{g,n} with image M^4 \ M^3. The Casnati–Ekedahl structure theorem attaches to a degree 4 cover a rank 3 bundle E and a rank 2 bundle F on P^1, both of degree g + 3, with det E ≅ det F, giving a map H_{4,g} → B to the moduli stack of such pairs and an embedding of the universal curve into P E^∨.
items.note: The structure theory of degree 4 covers, in the marked version needed here.

items.name: Pushforward of classes from the Casnati–Ekedahl projective bundle
items.statement: If x ∈ A^*(H^◇_{4,g,n}) lies in the image of A^*((P E^∨)^n) → A^*(H^◇_{4,g,n}), then β'_{n*}x is tautological on M_{g,n} \ M^3_{g,n}.
items.note: The criterion that converts Chow-ring generation upstairs into tautological classes downstairs.

items.name: The splitting-type stratification of H_{4,7,n}
items.statement: The splitting types E = O(e_1) ⊕ O(e_2) ⊕ O(e_3) and F = O(f_1) ⊕ O(f_2) stratify H_{4,7,n} as X_n ⊔ Y_n ⊔ Z_n, where X_n is the locus with E = (3,3,4) and F = (5,5) or (4,6); Y_n = Σ_{2,n} ⊔ Σ_{3,n} with Σ_{2,n} the locus E = (2,4,4), F = (4,6) and Σ_{3,n} the locus E = (2,3,5), F = (4,6); and Z_n the maximally unbalanced locus, which parametrises hyperelliptic curves and maps into M^3_{7,n}.
items.note: The explicit stratification in which the tetragonal case is checked.

items.name: The open stratum X_n
items.statement: For n ≤ 3, X_n has the CKgP and A^*((P E^∨)^n) → A^*(X_n) is surjective.
items.note: Quoted from Canning–Larson with g = 7 and f = f_1 = 4.

items.name: Presentation of the Chow rings of the Σ-strata
items.statement: For ℓ = 2, 3 and n ≤ 3 there is a surjection A^*(Σ_ℓ)[z_1, …, z_n, ζ_1, …, ζ_n] → A^*(Σ_{ℓ,n}) induced by Σ_{ℓ,n} → Σ_ℓ and restriction from (P E^∨)^n, where z_i and ζ_i are the pullbacks of c_1(O_P(1)) and c_1(O_{P E^∨}(1)) from the i-th factor; moreover Σ_{ℓ,n} has the CKgP.
items.note: The marked version of the stratum analysis of Canning–Larson.

items.name: The tetragonal locus has the CKgP
items.statement: For n ≤ 3, H^◇_{4,7,n} has the CKgP; hence M^4_{7,n} has the CKgP.
items.note: Combines Lemmas 5.2 and 5.3 with Proposition 4.2(2) and (3).

items.name: Restriction to the Σ-strata is surjective
items.statement: For ℓ = 2, 3 and n ≤ 3, the restriction A^*((P E^∨)^n) → A^*(Σ_{ℓ,n}) is surjective.
items.note: The Chow-ring generation needed to apply Lemma 5.1 on the Y-strata.

items.name: Generation of the Chow ring of the tetragonal Hurwitz stack
items.statement: For n ≤ 3, the pullback A^*((P E^∨)^n) → A^*(H^◇_{4,7,n}) is surjective.
items.note: Assembled from Lemmas 5.2 and 5.5 by excision.

items.name: Classes supported on the tetragonal locus are tautological
items.statement: If n ≤ 3, all classes in A^*(M_{7,n}) supported on M^4_{7,n} \ M^3_{7,n} are tautological.
items.note: The conclusion of the tetragonal analysis, via Lemma 5.1.

items.name: The universal orthogonal Grassmannian has the CKgP
items.statement: The stack OG(5, V) ≅ [OG(5,10)/SO_10] over BSO_10 has the CKgP and its Chow ring is freely generated by the Chern classes of the universal rank 5 subbundle U. The proof identifies [OG(5,10)/SO_10] with BStab_U for the maximal parabolic Stab_U stabilising an isotropic 5-plane, shows that BGL_5 → BStab_U is an affine bundle, and applies Proposition 4.2(4), (6).
items.locator: arXiv:2307.08830v3 (25 October 2024), Lemma 5.8 (with Remark 5.9 identifying Stab_U ≅ G ⋊ GL_5 with G ≅ G_a^{10})
items.note: The equivariant Chow computation on which the pentagonal case rests.

items.name: Chow rings of orthogonal Grassmann bundles
items.statement: Let V be a rank 2ν vector bundle with quadratic form on X. (1) The rational Chow ring of OG(ν, V) is generated over A^*(X) by the Chern classes of the tautological subbundle. (2) If X has the CKgP then OG(ν, V) has the CKgP. The proof stratifies OG(ν, 2ν) by Schubert cells and uses the Giambelli formula of Kresch–Tamvakis, which requires rational coefficients since it divides by 2.
items.note: A general statement about orthogonal Grassmann bundles; SF.5 plans Chow groups with Chern classes and intersection products, and R09.1 the Grassmannians themselves, so this belongs with them rather than with the moduli of curves.

items.name: Fibre powers of the orthogonal Grassmannian
items.statement: For n ≥ 1 the n-fold fibre product OG(5, V)^n over BSO_10 has the CKgP and its Chow ring is generated by the Chern classes of the tautological subbundles U_1, …, U_n pulled back from the factors.
items.locator: arXiv:2307.08830v3 (25 October 2024), Corollary 5.11 (with Remark 5.12 on BSO_10 and Totaro's weak Chow–Künneth property)
items.note: The ambient stack for the marked Mukai construction.

items.name: Mukai's model of pentagonal genus 7 curves, with markings
items.statement: Mukai realises every curve of gonality exactly 5 and genus 7 as a linear section C = OG(5,10) ∩ P^6 in the spinor embedding OG(5,10) ↪ P^{15}, canonically embedded, and conversely; in families this gives M^◦_7 ≅ [(Gr(7, S^+) \ Δ)/SO_10], an open substack of the Grassmann bundle Gr(7, S^+) over BSO_10, with the tautological subbundle restricting to the dual of the Hodge bundle. With markings: let L = ι^*O_{P S^+}(−1) for the universal spinor embedding ι, let Z_n ⊂ OG(5, V)^n be the open locus where ⊕_i L_i → π_n^*S^+ has rank n, and Q_n the cokernel, a rank 16 − n bundle on Z_n; then Gr(7 − n, Q_n) parametrises the P^6 containing the n given points.
items.note: The new construction of the paper: a marked version of Mukai's model, needed because the numerics of degree 5 covers defeat the Hurwitz-space technique with markings.

items.name: The pentagonal locus with markings has the CKgP
items.statement: For n ≤ 4 there is an open embedding α_n of M^◦_{7,n} into the Grassmann bundle Gr(7 − n, Q_n) over Z_n ⊂ OG(5, V)^n; hence M^◦_{7,n} has the CKgP. The embedding uses that for n ≤ 4 the images of the n sections under the canonical embedding are independent, since a dependency would give a g^1_n on a curve of gonality 5.
items.note: The geometric heart of Theorem 1.10.

items.name: Tautological identification of the pulled-back bundles
items.statement: With f : C → M^◦_{7,n} the universal curve and σ_i the i-th section, α_n^*U_i sits in an exact sequence 0 → α_n^*U_i → Sym^2 f_*(ω_f(−σ_i)) → f_*((ω_f(−σ_i))^{⊗2}) → 0; in particular every class pulled back from OG(5, V)^n to M^◦_{7,n} is tautological.
items.note: Identifies the abstract bundles of the Mukai model with tautological ones.

items.name: The tautological line bundles are the cotangent lines
items.note: The second identification needed for tautological generation.

items.name: The tautological subbundle on the Grassmann bundle
items.statement: For E_n the tautological rank 7 − n subbundle on Gr(7 − n, Q_n), the pullback α_n^*E_n sits in an exact sequence 0 → ⊕_{i=1}^n α_n^*L_i → (f_*ω_f)^∨ → α_n^*E_n → 0; in particular the Chern classes of α_n^*E_n are tautological.
items.note: Completes the identification of the generators with tautological classes.

items.name: The Chow ring of the pentagonal locus is tautological
items.statement: The Chow ring of M^◦_{7,n} is generated by tautological classes.
items.note: With Lemma 5.7 and the hyperelliptic–trigonal case this proves Theorem 1.10.

items.name: Proof that H^4 is tautological
items.statement: H^k(M̄_{g,n}) is tautological for k ≤ 3 by Arbarello–Cornalba; Theorem 1.3 then puts H^4(M̄_{g,n}) in the STE generated by H^4(M̄_{g',n'}) with g' < 7 and n' ≤ 4, and Proposition 4.5 shows W_4H^4(M_{g',n'}) is tautological in that range.
items.locator: arXiv:2307.08830v3 (25 October 2024), Proof of Theorem 1.5(1) in Section 6.1
items.note: The three-line proof that the explicit bounds of Theorem 1.3 make possible.

items.name: Proof that H^6 is tautological for g ≥ 10
items.statement: By Theorem 1.5(1) and Arbarello–Cornalba all classes in H^6(M̄_{g,n}) pushed forward from the boundary are tautological, and H^6(M_{g,n}) is stable, hence tautological, for g ≥ 10.
items.locator: arXiv:2307.08830v3 (25 October 2024), Proof of Theorem 1.5(2) in Section 6.1
items.note: Shows where the bound g ≥ 10 comes from.

items.name: What would settle degree six
items.statement: By Lemma 3.1 it suffices to prove that H^6(M̄_{g,n}) is tautological for g ≤ 9 and n ≤ 6; since H_6(M̄_{g,n}) is tautological by Theorem 1.5(3), it would suffice that the pairing RH^6(M̄_{g,n}) × RH_6(M̄_{g,n}) → Q be perfect there, which is in principle computable with admcycles but is too memory-intensive in practice.
items.note: Records the precise finite computation that would close the gap.

items.name: Vanishing of low-degree Borel–Moore homology of M_{g,n}
items.statement: For g ≥ 1, H^{BM}_k(M_{g,n}) = 0 for k < 2g when n = 0, 1 and for k < 2g − 2 + n when n ≥ 2 (Bergström–Faber–Payne, by duality with H^k_c).
items.locator: arXiv:2307.08830v3 (25 October 2024), Proof of Theorem 1.5(3) in Section 6.2
items.note: The vanishing that reduces each homological induction to finitely many (g, n).

items.name: Proof that low even homology is tautological
items.statement: Combining the Borel–Moore vanishing with the boundary sequence reduces to k ≥ 2g with n = 0, 1 or k ≥ 2g − 2 + n with n ≥ 2; for g ≥ 3 all such cases with k ≤ 14 have the CKgP and A^* = R^*, so W_{-k}H^{BM}_k(M_{g,n}) is tautological by Proposition 4.5; genus 1 is Petersen's theorem that all even cohomology is tautological, and genus 2 is Corollary 2.7.
items.locator: arXiv:2307.08830v3 (25 October 2024), Proof of Theorem 1.5(3) in Section 6.2
items.note: The inductive scheme used for all three homological theorems.

items.name: Degree 2d − 14 motivic structure
items.statement: As Hodge structures or Galois representations, H^{2d_{g,n}-14}(M̄_{g,n})^{ss} ≅ ⊕ L^{d_{g,n}-7}.
items.note: Poincaré duality applied to Theorem 1.5(3) for k = 14; the second statement of Theorem 1.1.

items.name: The genus two base case in degree 13 with eleven markings
items.statement: H^{13}(M̄_{2,11}) lies in the STE generated by H^{11}(M̄_{1,11}).
items.note: Proved from the authors' earlier theorem that H^{11}(M̄_{g,n}) lies in that STE, the CKgP for M_{2,10}, and Lemma 3.2 for the odd number of markings.

items.name: Proof of the thirteenth-homology theorem
items.statement: The Borel–Moore vanishing reduces to 13 ≥ 2g with n = 0, 1 or 13 ≥ 2g − 2 + n with n ≥ 2; all such (g, n) outside Z = {(2,11), (1,11), (1,12), (1,13)} have the CKgP, so W_{-13}H^{BM}_{13}(M_{g,n}) = 0 by Proposition 4.5; the case (2,11) is Lemma 7.1 with hard Lefschetz and the genus one cases follow from Proposition 2.2.
items.locator: arXiv:2307.08830v3 (25 October 2024), Proof of Theorem 1.6 in Section 7.1
items.note: The exceptional set Z is exactly where the CKgP is unavailable.

items.name: Degree 2d − 13 motivic structure
items.statement: As Hodge structures or Galois representations, H^{2d_{g,n}-13}(M̄_{g,n})^{ss} ≅ ⊕ L^{d_{g,n}-12} S_12 for all g and n.
items.note: The first statement of Theorem 1.1, after Poincaré duality.

items.name: The genus two base case in degree 15 with twelve markings
items.statement: H^{15}(M̄_{2,12}) is generated by classes pushed forward from the boundary; hence it is contained in the STE generated by H^{11}(M̄_{1,11}).
items.note: The hardest base case: Bergström–Faber's implementation of the Getzler–Kapranov formula gives H^{15}(M̄_{2,12})^{ss} = 836 L^2 S_12, and the proof exhibits 836 independent boundary pushforwards among 891 explicitly drawn decorated graphs, with 55 relations.

items.name: ω-decorated graphs and their conventions
items.statement: A decoration ω ∈ H^{11}(M̄_{1,11}) ≅ S_12 on a genus 1 vertex, pulled back along forgetful maps, together with a stable graph, determines by gluing pushforward a morphism L^e S_12 → H^{11+2e}(M̄_{g,n}) where e is the number of edges; a collection of such graphs 'is a basis for H^k(M̄_{g,n})' when the corresponding morphisms form a basis of Hom(L^e S_12, H^k(M̄_{g,n})) and H^k(M̄_{g,n}) ≅ Hom(L^e S_12, H^k) ⊗ L^e S_12. In the pictures a white vertex has genus 1, a black vertex genus 0, undrawn markings sit on the leftmost genus 1 vertex, and ω_i, ω_{ij} denote pullbacks of ω forgetting the indicated markings.
items.locator: arXiv:2307.08830v3 (25 October 2024), Section 7.2, conventions before Lemma 7.4
items.note: The calculus in which the explicit bases of Lemmas 7.4–7.7 and the 891-graph computation are expressed.

items.name: A basis for H^{13}(M̄_{1,12})
items.statement: The 11 ω-decorated graphs drawn in the paper form a basis for H^{13}(M̄_{1,12}).
items.note: One of the four explicit bases needed for the pairing computation of Lemma 7.3.

items.name: A basis for H^{13}(M̄_{1,13})
items.statement: The 429 ω-decorated graphs drawn in the paper form a basis for H^{13}(M̄_{1,13}); here x, y are any two markings and in the last group of classes i or j may equal y.
items.note: An explicit basis with its combinatorial description.

items.name: A basis for H^{13}(M̄_{1,14})
items.statement: For a set {x, y, 1, …, 12} of 14 markings, the 6006 ω-decorated graphs drawn in the paper form a basis for H^{13}(M̄_{1,14}); in the last grouping i, j or k may equal y.
items.note: The largest of the explicit bases.

items.name: A basis for H^{13}(M̄_{2,12})
items.statement: The 264 ω-decorated graphs drawn in the paper form a basis for H^{13}(M̄_{2,12}).
items.note: The genus two basis used to compute the pairings in Lemma 7.3.

items.name: Graphical presentations and the forthcoming complete list of relations
items.statement: Theorem 1.6 gives H_{13}(M̄_{g,n}) a graphical presentation with generators the decorated graphs of Lemmas 7.4–7.7; the authors announce forthcoming work proving that H^{13}(M̄_{g,n}) also lies in this STE, with a complete list of relations among the generators.
items.note: Records what is proved here and what is deferred.

items.name: An alternative route to the rank computation
items.statement: One could instead prove that the 891 classes span a space of rank 836 by computing the pairing of that space against itself, which by the argument of Lemma 7.3 must have rank 836.
items.note: The alternative computation, recorded for reproducibility.

items.name: The genus two base case with thirteen markings
items.statement: H^{15}(M̄_{2,13}) lies in the STE generated by H^{11}(M̄_{1,11}).
items.note: The second genus two base case for Theorem 1.7, obtained from Lemma 7.3 and Lemma 3.2.

items.name: Degree 2d − 15 motivic structure
items.statement: As Hodge structures or Galois representations, H^{2d_{g,n}-15}(M̄_{g,n})^{ss} ≅ ⊕ L^{d_{g,n}-13} S_12 ⊕ ⊕ L^{d_{g,n}-15} S_16 for all g and n.
items.note: The homological form of the degree 15 statement, before the S_16 terms are eliminated for g ≥ 2 in Section 8.

items.name: Conjecture on the fifteenth cohomology
items.statement: The STE generated by H^{11}(M̄_{1,11}) contains H^{15}(M̄_{g,n}) for g ≥ 2.
items.note: The cohomological strengthening of Theorem 1.7 for g ≥ 2, consistent with Theorem 1.1.

items.name: Genus two fifteenth homology
items.statement: The STE generated by H^{11}(M̄_{1,11}) contains H_{15}(M̄_{2,n}) for all n; hence H^{15}(M̄_{2,n})^{ss} ≅ ⊕ L^2 S_12 as Galois representations or Hodge structures.
items.note: The genus two case of the last statement of Theorem 1.1, obtained by comparing Theorem 1.7 with Corollary 2.9.

items.name: The weight 15 complex and its first two maps
items.statement: For g ≥ 3 one studies H^{15}(M̄_{g,n}) →^α ⊕_{|E(Γ)|=1} H^{15}(M̄_Γ)^{Aut(Γ)} → ⊕_{|E(Γ)|=2} (H^{15}(M̄_Γ) ⊗ det E(Γ))^{Aut(Γ)}, where Γ runs over stable graphs of genus g with n legs, the first map is pullback to the normalised boundary and the second is the differential of the weight spectral sequence described in the authors' earlier paper.
items.note: The complex in which the absence of S_16 for g ≥ 3 is verified.

items.name: Injectivity of the boundary pullback
items.statement: If g ≥ 3 then the pullback map α in the weight 15 complex is injective, because gr^W_{15}H^{15}_c(M_{g,n}) = 0: this holds whenever 2g − 2 + n > 15 by Bergström–Faber–Payne, and otherwise M_{g,n} has the CKgP, so Proposition 4.5 applies.
items.note: The step where the genus 7 base cases of Theorem 1.10 are needed.

items.name: The Hodge-theoretic vanishing of S_16 for g ≥ 3
items.statement: For g ≥ 3 the induced map β on the (15, 0) parts of the weight 15 complex is injective: graphs with a loop contribute H^{15,0}(M̄_{g-1,n+2}) = 0 by induction, and for a graph Γ with two vertices the only nonvanishing contribution is H^{15,0}(M̄_{1,A^c ∪ q}) with |A^c| ≥ 14, which injects into the corresponding summand for the graph Γ' obtained by adding a loop on the genus g − 1 vertex. Hence Theorem 1.1 holds in the category of Hodge structures.
items.note: The inductive graph argument that kills the S_16 contribution.

items.name: Splitting of H^{15}(M̄_{1,15})
items.statement: Let V ⊂ H^{15}(M̄_{1,15}) be the classes pushed forward from the boundary and W the image of H^{15}_c(M_{1,15}) → H^{15}(M̄_{1,15}). Then H^{15}(M̄_{1,15}) = V ⊕ W as Hodge structures and as Galois representations, with W ≅ S_16 and V^{ss} ≅ 186263 L^2 S_12. The proof uses that the Poincaré pairing is nondegenerate, that the inclusion of W is dual to the quotient onto W_{15}H^{15}(M_{1,15}) ≅ S_16, and that V has Hodge type (13,2) + (2,13) while W has type (15,0) + (0,15), so the pairing between them vanishes; the multiplicity 186263 is read off from Getzler.
items.note: The decomposition that transfers the Hodge-theoretic result to Galois representations.

items.name: Passage from Hodge structures to Galois representations
items.statement: By Poincaré duality it suffices to show that for g ≥ 2 no copies of L^{d_{g,n}-15} S_16 appear in Corollary 7.11. The proof of Theorem 1.7 presents H^{2d_{g,n}-15}(M̄_{g,n}) as a quotient of ⊕ L^{d-13} ⊗ H^{11}(M̄_{1,11}) ⊕ ⊕ L^{d-15} ⊗ H^{15}(M̄_{1,15}) by maps that are forgetful pullbacks followed by gluing pushforwards; by Lemma 8.3 it suffices that each such map vanish on L^{d-15} ⊗ W, which holds because the corresponding map of Hodge structures vanishes by the already proved Hodge-theoretic case, hence so does the map of Q-vector spaces and therefore of Galois representations.
items.locator: arXiv:2307.08830v3 (25 October 2024), End of Section 8 (proof of Theorem 1.1)
items.note: The final step: a Hodge-theoretic vanishing forces the Galois-theoretic one because both are computed by the same maps of Q-vector spaces.

items.name: Cusp forms for SL_2(Z)
items.statement: For an even weight k, S_k(SL_2(Z)) is the space of holomorphic cusp forms of weight k and level one; the paper uses that H^{k,0}(M̄_{1,k}) is the space of cusp forms of weight k + 1, so that H^{11,0}(M̄_{1,11}) is spanned by the discriminant form of weight 12.
items.locator: arXiv:2307.08830v3 (25 October 2024), Remark 2.5 and the definition of S_12
items.note: Mathlib has modular and cusp forms for a subgroup of GL_2(R) acting on the upper half plane, with the slash action; the identification with the Hodge groups of M̄_{1,k} is not in the libraries and is not planned in the atlas.

items.name: Projective and Grassmann bundles
items.statement: For a vector bundle E on a base, P E and the Grassmann bundle Gr(r, E) are the parameter spaces of rank one quotients and rank r subbundles, with their tautological sub- and quotient bundles and universal properties; the paper works with P E^∨ over the Casnati–Ekedahl base and with Gr(7 − n, Q_n) over Z_n.
items.note: R09.1 plans projective bundles, Grassmannians and flag schemes with their universal properties, universal sheaves and base change; Mathlib has the Grassmannian functor of rank n quotients of a module (Module.Grassmannian) but not these bundles over stacks.

prerequisites.citation: Gaëtan Chenevier, Jean Lannes, Automorphic forms and even unimodular lattices, Ergebnisse der Mathematik 69, Springer (2019)
prerequisites.why: Theorem F of loc. cit. lists the ℓ-adic Galois representations and Hodge structures of motivic weight ≤ 22 that can occur, which is the prediction Theorem 1.1 confirms in weights 13, 14 and 15.

prerequisites.citation: Samir Canning, Hannah Larson, Sam Payne, Extensions of tautological rings and motivic structures in the cohomology of M̄_{g,n}: the eleventh cohomology (H^{11}(M̄_{g,n}) and the weight 11 complex)
prerequisites.why: The authors' earlier paper, which proves that H^{11}(M̄_{g,n}) lies in the STE generated by H^{11}(M̄_{1,11}) and constructs the weight 11 complex whose weight 15 analogue is used in Section 8.

prerequisites.citation: Samir Canning, Hannah Larson, The Chow rings of the moduli spaces of curves of genus 7, 8, and 9
prerequisites.why: The stratification of H_{4,7} by Casnati–Ekedahl splitting types that Section 5.2 carries out with markings.

prerequisites.citation: Samir Canning, Hannah Larson, Chow rings of low-degree Hurwitz spaces / the CKgP for M_{g,n} in low genus
prerequisites.why: The source of the Chow–Künneth generation Property technique, of the filling criteria that Lemma 2.1 imitates, of Lemma 5.1, and of most entries of the table of known CKgP cases.

prerequisites.citation: Jonas Bergström, Carel Faber, Sam Payne, Polynomial point counts and odd cohomology vanishing on moduli spaces of stable curves, Ann. of Math. 199 (2024)
prerequisites.why: Proposition 2.1 of loc. cit. is the vanishing of low-degree Borel–Moore homology of M_{g,n} on which every induction in Sections 6–8 rests.

prerequisites.citation: Ezra Getzler, The semi-classical approximation for modular operads, Comm. Math. Phys. 194 (1998)
prerequisites.why: The classification of the pure cohomology of M_{1,n} quoted as Proposition 2.2 and the multiplicity 186263 in Lemma 8.3.

prerequisites.citation: Dan Petersen, Cohomology of local systems on the moduli of principally polarized abelian surfaces / on M_2 and M_{2,n}
prerequisites.why: The genus two results quoted as Propositions 2.6 and 2.8.

prerequisites.citation: Dan Petersen, Orlando Tommasi, The Gorenstein conjecture fails for the tautological ring of M̄_{2,n}, Invent. Math. 196 (2014)
prerequisites.why: With Graber–Pandharipande it shows that the bound k ≤ 20 in Conjecture 1.8 is the best possible.

prerequisites.citation: Dan Petersen, Orlando Tommasi, Yin Qizheng (Petersen–Tommasi–Yin), Tautological rings of fibered powers of the universal curve
prerequisites.why: The Leray/Künneth analysis of H^*(C^n) over M_g and the projectors used in the proof of Lemma 3.1.

prerequisites.citation: Shigeru Mukai, Curves and symmetric spaces I/II (the genus 7 case)
prerequisites.why: Theorem 0.4 and Proposition 2.2 of loc. cit. realise pentagonal genus 7 curves as linear sections of OG(5,10) in its spinor embedding, the construction extended with markings in Section 5.3.

prerequisites.citation: Gianfranco Casnati, Torsten Ekedahl, Covers of algebraic varieties I: a general structure theorem, J. Algebraic Geom. 5 (1996)
prerequisites.why: The structure theorem for degree 4 covers that produces the bundles E and F used throughout Section 5.2.

prerequisites.citation: Enrico Arbarello, Maurizio Cornalba, Calculating cohomology groups of moduli spaces of curves via algebraic geometry, Publ. Math. IHÉS 88 (1998)
prerequisites.why: The tautological computation of H^k(M̄_{g,n}) for k ≤ 3 and the inductive method whose degree 4 prediction Theorem 1.5(1) confirms.

prerequisites.citation: Nathalie Wahl, Homological stability for the mapping class group of orientable surfaces (and Harer's stability theorem)
prerequisites.why: Tautological generation of H^{k}(M_{g,n}) in the stable range k ≤ (2g − 2)/3, one of the three inputs to Theorem 1.3.

prerequisites.citation: Dan Edidin, William Graham, Equivariant intersection theory, Invent. Math. 131 (1998); Andrew Kresch, Cycle groups for Artin stacks, Invent. Math. 138 (1999)

routes.title: Tautological rings and motivic structures in the cohomology of moduli of stable curves
routes.brief: Plan the cohomology of the moduli spaces of stable curves and the motivic structures in it, following Canning, Larson and Payne. The final theorems are: (1) their Theorem 1.1: for all g and n, H^{13}(M̄_{g,n})^{ss} ≅ ⊕ L·S_12 and H^{14}(M̄_{g,n})^{ss} ≅ ⊕ L^7, and for g ≥ 2, H^{15}(M̄_{g,n})^{ss} ≅ ⊕ L^2·S_12, where L = H^2(P^1) and S_12 = H^{11}(M̄_{1,11}); (2) their Theorem 1.3: for each k, the semi-tautological extension generated by {H^{k'}(M̄_{g',n'}) : k' ≤ k, g' < (3/2)k' + 1, n' ≤ k', 4g' − 4 + n' ≥ k'} contains H^k(M̄_{g,n}) for all g and n, so only finitely many simple motives occur in each degree; (3) their Theorem 1.5: the tautological ring contains H^4(M̄_{g,n}) for all g and n, H^6(M̄_{g,n}) for g ≥ 10, and H_k(M̄_{g,n}) for even k ≤ 14; (4) their Theorems 1.6 and 1.7: H_{13}(M̄_{g,n}) lies in the semi-tautological extension generated by H^{11}(M̄_{1,11}), and H_{15}(M̄_{g,n}) in the one generated by H^{11}(M̄_{1,11}) and H^{15}(M̄_{1,15}); and (5) their Theorem 1.10: for n ≤ 3 the moduli space M_{7,n} has the Chow–Künneth generation Property and R^*(M_{7,n}) = A^*(M_{7,n}). The roadmap must cover, in order: the moduli stacks M_{g,n} and M̄_{g,n} as smooth proper Deligne–Mumford stacks with their boundary stratification by stable graphs, the tautological morphisms, the tautological rings and the ψ-, κ- and Hodge classes; the right-exact boundary sequences in cohomology and in Borel–Moore homology, with the subspaces Φ and Ψ and the partial order on (g, n); semi-tautological extensions, their closure properties, finite generation and the filling criterion; the decomposition of the pure cohomology of M_{g,n} in terms of symplectic local systems on M_g, with the genus one classification of Getzler and the genus two results of Petersen; the Chow–Künneth generation Property with its permanence properties and the theorem that it makes W_kH^k algebraic, in both the Hodge and the ℓ-adic realisation; the genus seven geometry — the gonality stratification, Hurwitz stacks of tetragonal covers with the Casnati–Ekedahl bundles, the orthogonal Grassmannian OG(5,10) with its spinor embedding, and the marked Mukai model of pentagonal curves; and finally the graphical calculus of ω-decorated graphs with the explicit bases and pairing computations in low genus, leading to the four main theorems. Import, and do not re-plan: stable pointed curves, nodes, dual graphs and marked stabilisation from the Tau Ceti roadmap Stable reduction, Layers 1, 3 and 9; algebraic stacks, coarse spaces and rigidification from Algebraic moduli for arithmetic geometry (AlgebraicModuliForArithmeticGeometry), stages R09.1 (projective and Grassmann bundles), R09.4 and R09.5; Chow groups, Chern classes and intersection products from Scheme and stack foundations (SchemeAndStackFoundations), stage SF.5, and sheaf cohomology with compact support and duality from SF.2; cycle class maps and realisations from Motives and algebraic cycles (MotivesAndAlgebraicCycles), stages MC.0 and MC.2; pure and mixed Hodge structures, polarisation and strictness from the Tau Ceti roadmap Hodge structures, Layers L0–L2; hard Lefschetz from Deligne weights and purity (DeligneWeightsAndPurity), stage DWP.9; and the Galois representations attached to level-one cusp forms from Automorphic Galois representations (AutomorphicGaloisRepresentations), stage R19.1. Two inputs the paper quotes are large enough to deserve their own layers rather than a citation: the virtual cohomological dimension 4g − 4 + n of M_{g,n} together with Harer's stability and Wahl's theorem in the stable range, and the vanishing of the low-degree Borel–Moore homology of M_{g,n} proved by Bergström–Faber–Payne.
routes.reason: The atlas has no moduli of curves at all: searches of every stage description return no hit for 'moduli of curves', 'M_{g,n}', 'tautological ring', 'tautological class', 'Chow ring', 'cycle class map', 'Borel–Moore', 'Brill–Noether' or 'symplectic local system'. The nearest layers are the Tau Ceti Stable reduction roadmap, which plans stable pointed curves but not their moduli stack; AlgebraicModuliForArithmeticGeometry, which plans Hilbert schemes, algebraic stacks and coarse spaces for the generalised elliptic curve and polarised abelian scheme problems; and MotivesAndAlgebraicCycles, which plans cycles and realisations. Nothing goes in the direction of the cohomology of M̄_{g,n}, so this is a new roadmap rather than a Part II, and it imports the stack, intersection-theoretic, Hodge-theoretic and Galois-theoretic infrastructure from the layers named in the brief.

SF.5 constructs Chow groups, rational equivalence, proper pushforward, flat and lci pullback, refined Gysin maps, Chern classes and intersection products. Two items of the extraction are general facts of that layer rather than facts about moduli of curves: the extension of the Chow groups to algebraic stacks stratified by quotient stacks, with excision and the exterior product A_*(X) ⊗ A_*(Y) → A_*(X × Y) — the setting in which the Chow–Künneth generation Property is even stated — and the computation of the rational Chow ring of an orthogonal Grassmann bundle from Schubert cells and the Kresch–Tamvakis Giambelli formula, which needs rational coefficients. The paper is a source for both, and the new roadmap imports them.

MC.2 constructs realisation functors and proves that cycle classes respect composition, cup products, pushforward, trace and Tate twists. The cycle class map this paper needs is the one for a smooth but not necessarily proper variety or Deligne–Mumford stack, landing in the lowest weight part W_{2i}H^{2i}, with the consequence that algebraic classes are of Hodge type (p, p) and Tate on the ℓ-adic side. That is the same map in the generality the moduli application requires, so it belongs to MC.2 and the paper is a source for it.

sourceIssues.reason: Theorem 1.5(3) states that RH^*(M̄_{g,n}) contains H_k(M̄_{g,n}) for even k ≤ 14, and the proof itself uses the opposite inequality two sentences later: 'When g ≥ 3, in all of these cases with k ≤ 14 we know that M_{g,n} has the CKgP'. The proof is correct with k ≤ 14; with k ≥ 14 it would assert the statement in degrees where it is open (Conjecture 1.8 concerns even k ≤ 20) and where the table of known CKgP cases does not apply.
